summary: Release blocker for 3.2.0, found by tools/verify.sh --release: BUG-22, the report scrolling sideways on a plan with long free text. The carrier was a nowrap evidence chip holding an accepted commit's reason. Plain-text chips now wrap, and colspan detail cells wrap. A :has()-free rule keeps the full-run mark wrapping, so browsers without :has() keep the wrap they had. A bare-cell wrap rule was tried and removed: measured, it split ordinary title words mid-letter. tools/check-report-interactive.mjs now plants hostile content in every rendered table of every report it checks, opening closed disclosures to reach them, and fails on any title word split mid-letter above the narrow breakpoint. The phase review's high (the new leg failed on the scale demo) and med (the split words) were fixed by P120.2. Its lows and the residual (an unbroken token in a title still widens the page, closable only in the renderer) are recorded internally. The committed reports and screenshots are re-rendered with the fix.

tasks.description: Fix BUG-22. Rendered from this repository's own plan, the report scrolls sideways at 960-1152px (table.phases right@13685). That case must show the overflow red before the fix. Print the UI pin budget (tools/count-ui-pins.py) before starting. Run `node tools/check-report-interactive.mjs` on a fresh render of this repo's plan and of the demo, and report the exit codes.

outcome.technical:
Fixes BUG-22. Rendered from this repository's own plan, the report scrolled sideways at 833-1512px. The cause was not the phase summary. It was a `span.ptev` evidence chip with `white-space:nowrap` whose text is an accepted commit's free-text reason (`accepted <sha>: <reason>`), so one unbreakable line widened table.phases.

The fix is three rules, covering the class:
- tables.css: `:where(table.phases,table.data) td[colspan]{overflow-wrap:anywhere}` at every width.
- tables.css: plain-text cells (`td:not([class]):not(:has(*))`) wrap, above the 52rem breakpoint only. Below it the table already scrolls inside its own frame, and wrapping there split words mid-letter when measured.
- badges.css: `.ptev:not(:has(*)){white-space:normal}` lets a plain-text chip wrap, while chips built from pills or counts keep nowrap. The redundant `.ptev[data-fullrun]` rule is removed.

Pin css2's label and clauses now say this, and they tie the full-run claim to the rendered markup.

Regression cases live in tools/check-report-interactive.mjs, so every report it checks is covered:
- For each phases/data table, it plants copies of the table's first row carrying a very long summary and an unbroken token, plus a plain-text chip and a token chip. At every width on the ladder, it compares the page's scroll width with and without them.
- A second check fails if the planted rows never painted or never wrapped.

Red-first: the helper's verdict is could-not-prove, because playwright is missing in its throwaway tree (verbatim in the return). The orchestrator re-ran the executor's probe, scratchpad P120.1/mut.py: exit 0, with each of the three rules removed on its own turning the case red, and a detached or unpainted planting turning the second check red. A css2 mutation probe turns the pin red three ways.

Followers re-rendered in the same commit, so the committed pages carry the fix: examples/report.sh, docs/index.html as its byte copy, docs/demo-large.html, and the screenshots.

Fresh renders of this repo's plan and the demo pass the browser checker.
outcome.descriptive: The report no longer scrolls sideways on a plan with long free text, at any width, and the browser check now plants hostile content in every report it checks to keep it that way.

intentCheck.basis: orchestrator check: cause located (a nowrap evidence chip), class fixed with three rules; probe re-run, each rule removed turns the case red; followers re-rendered

tasks.title: the BUG-22 fix passes every shipped report and splits no title word
tasks.description: Fixes the P120 review's findings R1-R4 on the BUG-22 fix. (1) The hostile-content leg plants only into tables that are rendered, or opens each enclosing details for the measurement and restores it; it names skipped tables, and `painted` stays strict over what was planted. The checker must exit 0 on examples/acme-store/acme-store-audit.html, docs/index.html, docs/demo-large.html and a fresh render of this repo's plan. (2) The bare-cell wrap rule no longer starves free-text columns above 52rem. A new checker assertion holds that no visible task or bug title word splits mid-letter at any ladder rung above 52rem (hyphen breaks excluded), shown red against the current rule, and the comment says what the rule costs and where. (3) css2 binds the accepted-commit mark: it renders _tev_phase_marks with an acceptedCommits entry and asserts the span is bare text. (4) The full-run mark keeps a :has()-free wrap rule, or the fallback is documented. Re-render the followers is the orchestrator's job; do not capture.

outcome.technical:
Fixes P120-R1 to R4 on the BUG-22 fix.

R1: check-report-interactive's hostile leg (10b) opens each shut details ancestor before planting, marks it, and shuts it again afterwards. It skips a table that is still not rendered, or that has no body row or prose cell, and names each skip in a note. `painted` stays strict over what was planted. On demo-large the proposal table is now planted and painted.

R2: the bare-cell `overflow-wrap:anywhere` rule is removed rather than re-tuned. Over all four reports:
- min-width floors either overflowed or still split words;
- with no rule, real content was clean.
New leg 10a fails on any visible bare-text title word that changes line between two letters or digits at a ladder rung above 832px. A break after a hyphen, slash or colon does not count. 10a was red on all three shipped reports before the fix; the reviewer also saw it go red with the old rule injected (316 splits at 833px). Residual, stated in tables.css and recorded internally: an unbroken token longer than the window in a title still widens the page; only a renderer change can close that.

R3: css2 renders _tev_phase_marks with an acceptedCommits entry and asserts the accepted span is bare text.

R4: `.ptev[data-fullrun]{white-space:normal}` is restored beside the :has rule, with the fallback documented, and pinned by css3.

Followers re-rendered in the same commit:
- examples/report.sh;
- docs/index.html, as its byte copy;
- docs/demo-large.html;
- the screenshots.

The checker exits 0 on all three shipped reports (reviewer: 183/183/189 checks).

Red-first: could-not-prove by the helper. The fix run reported css3 failing, which an archive export does not reproduce; that is suspected to be the helper not copying a declared directory, recorded internally. The checker leg also needs playwright, which the throwaway lacks.

Mutation probe (scratchpad P120.2/mut.py), re-run by the orchestrator on demo-large: exit 0, all seven rows as expected.

Review round 2: lows only, recorded internally.
outcome.descriptive: The report fix now passes every published report, no longer breaks ordinary words in task titles, and keeps working in browsers without newer CSS selectors.
